statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend halt removes the price path that this score measures. Stress is 62 in the elevated band on carried energy and policy exposure, and Confidence is 88 on a complete verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and the same reading applies to each instrument. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 0.91% but 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a narrow 159-point cash range, and NQ's final tick of 29,391.75 was 108 points under a 29,499.50 high. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, exactly 24 hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract offers no interval to mark. Stress remains elevated and is the honest carrier of the weekend exposure: an offline Saudi bypass pipeline, crude near 100 dollars, and a Wednesday FOMC priced near certain to raise rates. That exposure reprices into a single Sunday opening print rather than into an intraday path, which is gap risk rather than Tail risk.
headline: A shut tape into the weekend: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but mid-range and 105 points below its high, CME futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC, and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage travels into a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range after opening at 29,331.48. The cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished 105 points below the high and 55 above the low, so the closing auction neither extended the advance nor broke it. NQ futures printed a final tick of 29,391.75, up 0.88%, some 108 points under a 29,499.50 session high and inside a wider 29,040.50 to 29,499.50 range that contains the pre-release repricing. VIX closed 15.84 after an 11.21% single-day decline, near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. Delayed cross-asset context collected before the halt showed seven of eight tracked megacaps higher and the semiconductor complex leading, several names up between 2% and 4%. Broad participation supports direction but is not by itself evidence of a path that denies mean reversion.

The macro backdrop is why Stress stays elevated while Tail does not. August CPI, released at 12:30 UTC, rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over twelve months, in line with expectations, while core CPI rose 0.3% against a 0.2% consensus. That core overshoot moved rate expectations sharply: futures ended the session pricing roughly an 87% probability of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC, up from about 72% a day earlier and about 50% a week before. The 10-year Treasury yield finished 4.975%, up 3.1 basis points and near the top of a 4.904 to 4.985 range; the most recent published H.15 2-year observation is 4.56% for 10 September. Equities rising while yields rise is cross-asset conflict rather than confirmation, and conflict of that kind belongs in Stress. Friday's gain also sits inside a negative week: the major indexes snapped a four-day decline but still finished the week lower.

Energy carries the largest unresolved exposure. WTI fell 2.43% on Friday to about 100 dollars and Brent to about 104 after reports that Iran and Gulf states would meet in Oman to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, yet crude still finished the week 9.7% higher. The reason is structural: the Strait has been effectively closed since the conflict that began in February, and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the principal bypass that reroutes roughly 5 million barrels a day to the Red Sea, was shut on Thursday after drone strikes on multiple pumping stations, with no published repair timeline. A diplomatic track and a damaged bypass point in opposite directions, which widens the distribution without establishing a direction.

The structural fact that dominates this horizon is simpler than any of it. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, exactly 24 hours after the last slot in this forecast. Every one of the twenty-four forward hours therefore describes a market in which no price can print on the reference contract, and a persistent no-retracement path is the thing Tail measures. Conditional Tail rests on a residual floor of 5 to 7 across the window, which allows for thin out-of-hours quoting on venues that price outside CME sessions rather than for any observed structure, and widens by one or two points only as the distance between Friday's verified evidence and the eventual reopen grows. Confidence opens at 88 on a complete verified closing set and decays into the high 70s at the far end for the same reason: the facts stay verified, but their power to describe a reopen a full day beyond the horizon falls as they age.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 23:00 UTC on 10 September to 22:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at Tail 14 in mixed mode and eases through the overnight to a low of 11 as Asian and early European trade stayed orderly, with Stress pinned in the middle eighties on the energy and policy backdrop. The mode turns trend-up from 06:00 to 11:00 UTC as the European session built a directional advance that still allowed retracement, Tail contained between 13 and 15. The only watch-band readings in the window are the two CPI hours: 12:00 UTC at Tail 21 with Confidence cut to 70, and 13:00 UTC at Tail 22 as Confidence recovered to 80, both labelled event/whipsaw. Tail then falls back to the mid-teens in mixed mode across the U.S. afternoon, and the final three hours mark the transition into the closure: 13 at 20:00 UTC as the cash close passed, 7 at 21:00 UTC as the CME halt took effect, and 6 at 22:00 UTC. Stress declines monotonically across the whole window from 86 to 64 as the event risk resolved into a completed session.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, exactly 24 hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot that contains observed rather than hypothetical structure, settles on a 5-point residual floor through the overnight and the middle of Saturday, widens to 6 from 13:00 UTC and to 7 from 19:00 UTC as the distance between Friday's verified evidence and the eventual reopen grows. That floor is a model allowance for thin out-of-hours quoting, not a forecast of structure, and the whole path stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green in all twenty-four slots. Stress eases from 62 to 58 through the dead middle of the closure and then rises to 64 into the final hours, because the unresolved threads compound toward one reopen: an offline Saudi bypass pipeline, a Hormuz arrangement still under negotiation, and an FOMC on 16 September priced near certain to raise rates into 3.4% headline inflation. Confidence decays from 88 to 79 purely on evidence age. The hours named for the Tokyo and London cash opens and the 12:30 UTC U.S. release slot are empty on a Saturday, which removes the handovers and the catalyst that most often build directional continuation.
